notes: v224 — the four v38 IN-HANDS failures, reproduction-first (tools/fix-batch-v224-test.js, 49/49: every item's failing field sequence built in the harness and watched RED before the fix). (1) LIVE-MILES-RESTORE-V38-FAIL: the v222 reseed adopted from the device store, but the store itself had already lost the day — the first pull's generic 'both changed, latest stamp wins' merge let a young engine's ~0.3 km snapshot (persisted minutes after the install, stamped NOW) outvote the cloud's whole day (stamped at its last push), and the flush then pushed the young record UP over the cloud. js/cloudsync.js: the telemetry keys (livemiles, geoloads) now merge DAY BY DAY ON TOTALS at pull time — each day keeps the record with the larger total (totalM / count+corr), ties to the later-updated record; the union stays dirty when it holds days the cloud lacks, so the flush carries the union up, never a young snapshot over a full day. The harness replays the stamp war end to end: pre-fix the engine held 0.33 km and the hero painted '0.3 km' (his screenshot exactly); post-fix the engine adopts the cloud's 138.5 km, the hero paints it, counting continues from it, and the pushed record carries the full day. The fresh-install sequence (empty store + cloud record) is asserted too and held throughout. (2) NAV-NO-MOVEMENT-V38: modules/navigator.js — the fallback stream's dedupe ran on a watermark BOTH streams stamped; the watch's device-clock stamps sat ahead of the app stream's GPS-clock stamps, so every stream fix read as 'already seen' and, with the watch dead in the background, the drive froze while the miles engine (same stream) kept counting. The dedupe is now the stream's OWN watermark (streamFixT): a stream fix is refused only when it repeats that stream's own last fix; the watchdog bridge feeds through the same rule. The harness models the field sequence (dispatch Navigate open, seeded last fix, timestamped watch fixes, watch death, live skewed stream) — RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix; same-fix and stale-fix refusals preserved. (3) BUBBLE-FACE-WRONG-OCT22 (web half): the bubble face now carries the owner's restated spec — timer, load count with the +/− correction buttons (wired to the dashboard's own load-correction actions), start/stop — and the face is swapped in BEFORE the window shrinks: js/shifttrack.js addPipWillEnterListener hears the shell's new 'pipWillEnter' event (native half ships in APK v39) and raises the face on it; the pipChanged path still confirms entry and restores on expand. Native halves (widget + bubble) ship in APK v39; this web version stands alone safely on v38 (the will-enter listener is simply never fired there).
